DNS: How google.com Becomes an IP Address: storyboard

Episode 9 · voice Liam · 9 scenes · 86.3s (measured timing) · one still per beat, 8 frames after it fires

hook hook Hook · 0.0s–8.5s

Headline: Lost by name

“Your phone has no idea where google.com is. It only understands numbers, so before a single byte loads, it has to look one up.”

branding sting 8.5s–10.0s

Bite wipe → logos → cut. No voiceover, just the chomp.

idea idea Transform · 10.0s–19.2s

Headline: Names in, digits out

“That lookup is DNS, the internet's phonebook: hand it a name, and it hands back an IP address, the number your phone actually dials.”

breakdown records Snippet · 19.2s–30.8s

Headline: The main records

“Each entry is a record: A holds the address, CNAME points to another name, MX handles email, and TXT carries notes, like proof you own the domain.”

breakdown walk Tree · 30.8s–41.4s

No headline

“None of that lives on your phone. It asks a recursive resolver, usually your provider's, which walks from the root, to dot com, to Google's own servers.”

breakdown answer Chat · 41.4s–52.1s

Headline: The source of truth

“Those authoritative servers own the answer. They send back the address, plus a TTL: how long anyone may keep that answer before asking again.”

breakdown propagation Timeline · 52.1s–62.1s

Headline: Why changes lag

“Resolvers cache it until that timer runs out, so repeat lookups are instant, but a changed record spreads slowly. That lag is propagation.”

breakdown cdn Split · 62.1s–71.6s

Headline: One name, many answers

“CDNs use this to route you: the same name, asked from Sydney or London, points each of you at a different server, the one nearest you.”

breakdown bigpicture BigPicture · 71.6s–80.8s

No headline

“You do all of this on every link you tap and every app you open, without ever noticing: ask, cache, route.”

gist gist GistCard · 80.8s–86.3s

No headline

“That's the gist: DNS turns names into numbers. Follow for more.”
